newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle bids early Thursday at $67.00 per cwt were passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00, steady with Wednesday's active sales, but down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 55,000 to 60,000 head sold Wednesday in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area and as many as 40,000 in Kansas, sources in those areas estimated.
"We could end up with more, at least in Kansas, because sales were so late that cattle are still being counted," one Kansas feedyard manager said.
Sales on Thursday were expected to be "clean-up" following Wednesday's brisk late afternoon trading, a Panhandle area cattle feeder said.
Fed cattle prices were pulled lower by slipping beef prices this week, sources said. Beef prices were pressured by increased tonnage following hefty cattle slaughter last week, they said.
USDA tabbed cattle kills last week at 737,000 head, above 703,000 a week earlier but just under 739,000 a year earlier.

Concern that Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report would be bearish also weighed on fed cattle prices, they said. The report is expected to show on-feed numbers and April placements well above last year, analysts projected.
